<explanation>
Based on the file tree and README information, Anx Reader is a cross-platform, Flutter-based e-book reader with rich features including AI-powered capabilities (supporting multiple AI services like OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), multi-format e-book parsing, note-taking, full synchronization (via WebDAV), and detailed analytics. The project targets multiple platforms (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Web) and follows a modular layered architecture to separate presentation, business logic, and data access.

Below are detailed instructions on how to draw an accurate system design diagram for Anx Reader:

1. Identify Main Components:
   • User Interface (UI) Layer: Represented by the Flutter components. In the "lib/page" and "lib/widgets" directories, you have pages for the homepage, settings, book player, reading view, and various UI controls for notes, customization, and statistics. This layer handles user interaction on all supported platforms.
   • Service/Business Logic Layer: Housed in subdirectories like "lib/service" and "lib/providers". This includes modules for AI integration (under “lib/service/ai”), book management, translation (using Google/Microsoft integrations), text-to-speech, file conversion (e.g., TXT and PDF conversion), synchronization, and statistical analysis.
   • Data Access Layer: Look in "lib/dao", which contains data access objects for books, book notes, reading times, and themes, and in "lib/config" for shared preferences. This layer manages local database operations and configuration settings.
   • External Integrations and APIs: External services such as WebDAV for syncing, AI services (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek), and translation APIs are integrated in the service modules.
   • Platform Specific Layers: Native directories (android, ios, macos, windows, linux, web) indicate that the app leverages platform-specific embedding and configuration using the Flutter engine. These directories form the bridge between the Flutter code and native platform capabilities.

2. Analyze Relationships & Interactions:
   • The UI layer (Flutter pages and widgets) interacts with the service layer via providers. For instance, a user action like highlighting a text or switching themes is propagated through UI widgets to the service modules.
   • The service modules implement the business logic. For example, the book player service communicates with the UI to render content, and the convert_to_epub service converts various formats.
   • The data access layer interacts with both UI (for local data display) and service modules (for updating state, persisting changes, and syncing).
   • External services (AI, translation, sync via WebDAV) are called from within respective service modules, and responses are then managed and passed back to the UI.
   • Additional configuration and logging utilities (found under “lib/utils” and “lib/providers”) assist in error handling, analytics, and version management.

3. Architectural Patterns and Design Principles:
   • The project is modular and adopts a layered (or MVVM/MVC-like) architecture where the presentation (UI) is decoupled from the business logic and data access.
   • Provider packages (Riverpod code generation is mentioned in the README) are used for state management and dependency injection, promoting clean separation of concerns.
   • Cross-platform design: Although Flutter manages the majority of the presentation, native directories handle platform-specific settings and adaptations.

4. Including Relevant Technologies:
   • Flutter & Dart as the main framework and language.
   • Riverpod for state management and code generation (indicated by usage of build_runner).
   • Native integration files for Android, iOS, etc., highlighting platform-specific adaptations.
   • Integrated AI and translation services with various submodules in the service layer.
   • File conversion libraries for EPUB, MOBI, PDF, TXT formats and web-based ebook renderers from “assets/foliate-js”.

5. Guidelines for Tailoring the Diagram:
   • For a full-stack-like application (even though this is a Flutter app, it behaves like a full stack with its layered architecture), clearly separate the presentation (UI), business logic, and data persistence layers.
   • Emphasize external API communication and integrations which are crucial for features like sync and AI assistance.
   • You could consider drawing a high-level diagram (overview showing the main layers and modules) and then a more detailed one zooming into key areas such as the book player and AI integration.

6. Suggested Diagram Elements:
   • Use clearly labeled boxes for key components: “UI Layer”, “Service/Business Logic Layer”, “Data Access Layer”, “External Services/APIs”, and “Platform/Native Integration”.
   • Use directional arrows to illustrate data flows and dependencies – for example, arrows from “UI” to “Service Layer” indicating user actions triggering logic, then further arrows from “Service Layer” to “Data Access” for persistence.
   • Utilize color coding or distinct shapes (e.g., cylinders for databases, parallelograms for external APIs) to indicate differences between components.
   • Optionally include a layer that denotes cross-platform integrations – showing that the “UI Layer” is rendered by Flutter but deployed on Android, iOS, macOS, etc.

7. Detailing Your Diagram:
   • Name each component explicitly using the folder structure as guidance (e.g., label “lib/page” as "UI Pages", “lib/service/ai” as "AI Services", “lib/dao” as "Data Access Objects", etc.).
   • Mark integration points (e.g., WebDAV sync, translation APIs) and annotate key functions like “TTS”, “Conversion Services”, and “Reading Analytics”.
   • Highlight modularity—note that improvements or changes in one module (like switching AI services) have minimal impact on others due to the clear layered separation.

By following these guidelines, the diagram will clearly capture both the breadth and the modular depth of Anx Reader’s architecture. This ensures that every aspect—from user interactions to underlying data processing and external service integrations—is represented, providing a complete and accurate view of the system.
</explanation>
